subject: Urgent: WebSocket token blackout and chunked-transfer resets across multiple customers

Date: Tue, 20 Jun 2028 14:12:00 -0400
Subject: Live feeds dropping (silent stream) — urgent

Hi Jasmine,

We're seeing a recurring problem on our live product feeds using Redwood streaming endpoints: the WebSocket connection stays open but tokenized output stops for 5–30s (clients report 'silent' periods), then resumes with a burst. The effect is effectively identical to a chunked-transfer reset — partial frames followed by silence. This is impacting our checkout personalization flow and increasing our latency and error rates significantly.

Observed impact (last 12h):
- 14% increase in stream timeouts from browser clients
- Several orders stalled due to downstream client-side timeouts
- Throughput drop: sustained 30% reduction in completed responses per second during blackout windows

Attached: ws_capture_0620.pcap (packet-level capture from a customer session), timestamps for two incidents.

We tried switching to non-streaming polling for a test shard but the extra request volume and latency is costly. We need immediate triage and an ETA for mitigation or a temporary workaround. Please escalate.

—Tim

Subject: Re: Live feeds dropping (silent stream) — triage notes

Quick triage notes after an initial look at the pcap and traces you gave us (thanks Tim).

Findings so far:
- TCP path looks healthy; no resets during the silence windows.
- Server continues to accept data and write to socket according to kernel stats, but clients report no application-level chunks for a window.
- Early suspicion: buffering in the HTTP ingress/proxy layer (Envoy/nginx) combined with a recent change to our tokenized chunk flush thresholds in the runtime (we lowered flush frequency to optimize small-token cost). The combination can produce 'silent' buffering periods then a burst when buffers flush.
- We also see correlation with higher-concurrency requests on certain pods (suggests per-worker batching/backpressure interactions).

Immediate mitigations we can try (low-risk):
1) Set proxy_buffering off and reduce proxy_read_timeout to 30s on affected ingress routes.
2) Re-enable a higher flush frequency for the runtime on a canary subset (increase flush to avoid large in-memory accumulation).
3) Divert impacted customers to a dedicated capacity pool (if approved by leadership) to both reduce noisy neighbor and allow different runtime tuning.

I've attached trace_dump_0620.txt with span ids for the blackout windows. We'll instrument more telemetry to capture per-token flush timings.

Action: will coordinate with infra to flip proxy buffering, roll the runtime flush change to a single canary, and report back within 90 minutes. Please let customers know we have mitigations in motion.

—Dev

Rishi / Leadership — escalating for visibility and decisioning. Multiple strategic customers (Acme Retail, BrightLeaf AI) are impacted by a streaming blackout pattern that maps to chunked-transfer buffering + runtime flush tuning. Triage notes and mitigations are below.

Summary:
- Impact: increased error rates (15–25% higher streaming errors), latency spikes, and a measurable throughput dip for streaming endpoints during blackout windows. Customers report client-visible stalls 5–30s.
- Root suspicion: interaction between ingress buffering (Envoy/nginx proxy settings) and a recent runtime optimization that reduced per-token flush frequency to lower cost.
- Mitigations in flight: ingress proxy_buffering disabled for affected routes (rolled), runtime flush frequency increased to canary (rolling), option to divert impacted customers to dedicated pool.

Decision asks:
1) Approve diversion of Acme & BrightLeaf to a short-lived dedicated capacity pool (estimate 4–12 hours) so we can revert/retune runtime without broad customer impact. This will have cost/operational implications and may require an exec sign-off for capacity.
2) Approve a customer remediation package — propose a service credit for the impacted windows and a post-mortem within 72 hours.

Attached artifacts: trace_dump_0620.txt, ws_capture_0620.pcap, mitigation_patch.diff. JIRA ticket: JIRA-INC-1428.

I'll coordinate the customer call at 17:00 ET and prepare a short slide for execs if helpful. Please advise ASAP so we can confirm the divert.

Thanks,
